# `max_consecutive_repeat` is blind to CYCLES — it scores a real loop LOWER than healthy breadth

## Context / Problem

The repetition detector shipped by [rebar:a89d-4dd2-f421-417a] reduces each tool call to a
`(tool_name, sha256(args)[:8])` signature and summarises the sequence
(`src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:213` `_repetition_summary`). Its headline loop signal is
**`max_consecutive_repeat`** — the longest run of *adjacent identical* signatures.

**Measured against three real traces of the same gate, that metric points the wrong way for cycles.**

| trace | what it is | overall distinct ratio | `max_consecutive_repeat` |
|---|---|---|---|
| bf31 pre-fix (264 calls) | a **genuine loop** — a closed 4-call cycle repeated 31-37x | 0.511 | **1** |
| c827 post-fix (258 calls) | **healthy breadth**, 92% distinct signatures | 0.922 | **5** |
| 46a2 / 94a3 close (260 calls) | a **genuine loop** — one identical call repeated 131x adjacently | 0.462 | 131 |

The 4-cycle scores **1**; the healthy run scores **5**. The reason is structural: bf31's
loop was a **cycle over four distinct calls**, so no two *adjacent* signatures are ever equal.
`max_consecutive_repeat` can only see a call repeated back-to-back — the degenerate 1-cycle. Any
cycle of length >= 2 is invisible to it. And ticket 46a2-9c1a-d855-4706's proposed trip
threshold of 5 sits exactly ON the healthy run's score — an actuator wired to this metric fires
on healthy runs and misses real cycles.

This is not academic. a89d's own conclusion — *"requests=240 tool_calls=475 distinct=451
max_consecutive_repeat=1 … It is NOT a runaway loop"* — was drawn from this metric, and bf31's
trace proves a run can be an unambiguous loop and still score 1.

## Approach

Add a windowed distinct-ratio to the summary `_repetition_summary` already produces — additive,
beside the existing counters, computed from the same signature list the function already receives,
so no caller changes and the sidecar contract only gains a field. Set-cardinality over a trailing
window divided by the window size is order-insensitive (robust to completion-order logging) and
catches every cycle length: measured over the three traces, `distinct(last 24)/24` reaches 0.167
on the bf31 4-cycle (fires at call 151 of 264), ~0.04 on the 46a2 adjacent repeat, and never drops
below **0.833** on the healthy run — a wide margin around the 0.50 trip line. Below the window the
field is `None` (insufficient sample — a 24-call minimum before any loop accusation is possible),
so consumers cannot false-trip on short runs. The window and
threshold live beside the producer as named constants because three consumers (this summary, the
c827 actuator, the aec1 recorder) must agree on one definition.

## The shared discriminator contract (consumed by [rebar:c827-2a23-cd00-473e] and [rebar:aec1-76e7-bb95-4c86])

| item | value |
|---|---|
| summary field name | `distinct_ratio_window` |
| window (trailing tool calls) | `24` (module constant `REPETITION_WINDOW`) |
| trip condition (consumers') | `distinct_ratio_window is not None and distinct_ratio_window <= 0.50` (module constant `REPETITION_TRIP_RATIO`) |
| semantics | set cardinality of tool-call signatures over the trailing `REPETITION_WINDOW` calls, divided by `REPETITION_WINDOW`; order-insensitive; rounded to 3 decimals |
| insufficient-sample rule | with fewer than `REPETITION_WINDOW` signatures (including the empty sequence) the field is `None` — too small a sample to accuse a loop, so consumers can never trip on it. This prevents the false positive where a short all-identical prefix (e.g. 2 identical calls / 2) reads as ratio 0.5 and trips at call 2; every real trip in the evidence fired at call 88+. |
| producer | `usage_log._repetition_summary` |

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py` — `_repetition_summary` gains `distinct_ratio_window`; the two
  named constants; `format_repetition` renders the new field.
- `tests/unit/test_usage_log_repetition_a89d.py` — the tests below. This is the existing suite for
  `_repetition_summary`/`failure_usage` (the repetition tests shipped by a89d live here, not in
  `tests/unit/test_usage_log.py`, whose subject is the recorder/aggregation surface).

This ticket is about the DETECTOR's signal quality only. It does not act on the signal —
that is [rebar:c827-2a23-cd00-473e]'s subject — but c827 cannot wire an actuator to a metric that
scores a loop below healthy work, so this is a prerequisite for any repetition-triggered remedy.

## Caveat on the evidence

The traces log tool calls in **completion** order, so adjacency-sensitive numbers carry some
uncertainty (the real detector reads emission order from the message list). That uncertainty applies
to the `max_consecutive_repeat` column and NOT to the distinct-ratio columns, which are
order-insensitive. The structural argument — a k-cycle with k >= 2 has no adjacent duplicates — holds
independently of ordering.

Evidence: `/tmp/bf31-trace-evidence.jsonl` (264 rows), `/tmp/c827-trace.jsonl` (258 rows), and the
46a2 telemetry line (`requests=240 tool_calls=260 distinct=120 max_consecutive_repeat=131`).

## Testing

    pytest tests/unit/test_usage_log_repetition_a89d.py -q

Happy path: a synthetic 4-cycle trips the new signal. Edge/failure paths: a high-novelty sequence
does not trip it; sequences shorter than the window report `None` (including an all-identical short
prefix, the false-trip shape); the empty sequence reports `None`; an adjacent-repeat run
(the 46a2 shape) trips it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `_repetition_summary` reports `distinct_ratio_window` with window `24`, computed as set
      cardinality of the trailing window's signatures divided by `REPETITION_WINDOW`, rounded to
      3 decimals; `None` when fewer than `REPETITION_WINDOW` signatures exist (including the empty
      sequence); verified by unit tests with hand-computed expected values
- [x] the window and trip threshold are module-level named constants (`REPETITION_WINDOW = 24`,
      `REPETITION_TRIP_RATIO = 0.50`) exported beside the producer; verified by a test importing
      them
- [x] a test replays a synthetic k-cycle (k = 4, >= 24 calls) and asserts
      `distinct_ratio_window <= 0.50` while `max_consecutive_repeat == 1`, so the blind spot is
      pinned rather than re-introduced
- [x] a test replays a high-novelty sequence (>= 24 distinct signatures) and asserts
      `distinct_ratio_window` stays above `0.50`
- [x] a test replays an adjacent-repeat run (one signature repeated >= 24x, the 46a2 shape) and
      asserts the signal trips
- [x] a test replays a short all-identical sequence (< 24 calls) and asserts the field is `None` —
      the false-trip shape a whole-sequence denominator would have produced
- [x] the existing counters keep their current meaning and field names (the sidecar contract is
      unchanged; `format_repetition` output still carries them); the new signal is additive;
      verified by the existing tests in `tests/unit/test_usage_log_repetition_a89d.py` passing
      unmodified
- [x] the privacy contract is unchanged — arguments stay hashed, never recorded; verified by the
      existing signature tests in that same file passing unmodified
